correctness.rationale: The order-polytope degree and vertex formulas are reconstructed from Stanley’s triangulation and vertex theorem. Toric orbit additivity gives Euler characteristic. The fence chain polytope is the path stable-set polytope by a lattice-affine equivalence. At an independent-set vertex S, the active-facet count is n+sum_{i in S}(deg(i)-1), so any selected interior path vertex forces nonsimplicity. The four endpoint-only vertices have primitive active normals of determinant ±1. The degree--Euler crossover is established at n=5,6 and propagated by an exact recurrence consequence of (sec z+tan z)'=(A^2+1)/2.

value.rationale: The finding gives a complete local classification at every torus fixed point of a natural infinite Hibi family studied in the singularity literature, not merely a numerical invariant. It reveals a strong saturation phenomenon: the number of fixed points grows Fibonacci-fast while the smooth fixed-point count stabilizes at four. The accompanying degree/Euler crossover at n=5 links the two classical fence sequences to distinct algebraic-geometric invariants and supplies a sharp phase boundary.
